newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Tension mounts in Albania as protests spread.
newsitem.headline: Tension mounts in Albania as protests spread.

text.p: Fresh protests spread across Europe's poorest nation on Sunday, with angry investors demanding compensation after pyramid investment schemes collapsed.
In a televised address, Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi promised his government would start paying back investors' savings in the get-rich-quick schemes from February onwards.

"With the preparations made so far we may start the systematic distribution of the money from about February 5," Meksi said, adding the government already had a stockpile of 30 billion leks ($300 million) from two pyramid schemes.
The pledge did little to subdue irate Albanians, many of whom have lost their life savings in schemes that offered very high interest on relatively small deposits.

In the town of Berat, 120 km (80 miles) south of Tirana where demonstrators set fire to the town hall, a police station and the prosecutor's office on Saturday, troops were out in force guarding other state institutions, witnesses said.
"Army troops were seen guarding the state institutions which were not burned last night," a witness said, adding people had started gathering in the centre of town.
Police in the capital Tirana were on alert on Sunday ahead of an opposition rally scheduled for 11 a.m. (1000 GMT). Road blocks were set up on routes into the capital, witnesses said.
"People are peacefully demonstrating in the streets today," another witness from Lushnje, 85 km south of Tirana, added by telephone.
Thousands were also reported to be gathering in the southern town of Vlore, 150 km (100 miles) from Tirana.
